summary: In this excerpt from Book 3, the narrator and her companion sit under a tropical starry sky and she recounts her investigation into Alex Goddard, Quetzal Manor, and Colonel Ramos, whom she suspects roughed up Lou and took Sarah. She believes the babies at Quetzal Manor are tied to Goddard's clinic, Ninos del Mundo, where Ramos may have taken Sarah. The companion calls it a case of selling kids, notes press stories about Americans accused of kidnapping Maya children for adoption, and warns about Guatemala's history of people being 'disappeared' by the Army in the late 1980s.
one_line: The narrator details her suspicions about Alex Goddard, Quetzal Manor, and Colonel Ramos in Guatemala, linking them to missing children and Sarah's disappearance.
key_facts: The narrator says she recounted her findings about Alex Goddard and Quetzal Manor to her companion.
The narrator says Colonel Ramos threatened her and Carly about her film.
The narrator believes Colonel Ramos and a couple of his goons roughed up Lou and took Sarah.
Sarah called the place Ninos del Mundo on her landing card.
The narrator believes Alex Goddard's clinic is tied to the scheme and that Ramos has taken Sarah there.
The companion says the situation sounds like a classic case of selling kids, a crime he puts up there with murder and grand larceny.
The companion notes press stories over the last few years about Americans attacked in Guatemala on suspicion of trying to kidnap Maya children for adoption.
The narrator says the babies she saw at Quetzal Manor are not kidnapped Indian children and are 'Caucasian as vanilla snow cones.'
A man at the embassy named Barry Morton told the narrator to be careful about turning over rocks in Guatemala.
The companion says Guatemala turned the word 'disappear' into a new kind of verb.
The companion says he knew some people who were 'disappeared' in the late eighties after an Army truck rolled into a village.
The companion says he has never seen proof of the kidnapping-for-adoption accusations against Americans.
